reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as an educational Dogcoin network review covering staking, token utility, chart analysis, and a purchase walkthrough, while directing viewers to do their own research. The 170% projection is conditional, and the available video evidence does not establish guaranteed returns, deceptive conduct, or a completed transfer. The separate cyber-community advertisement and exchange bonus link are not established as affiliated with the token walkthrough or as having caused harm.

citations.quote: DogCoin Network Full Review | Buy $DOGS on Pancakeswap
i will show you how you can buy the token
About 170% profit in the future
Ok, Now how to buy this token inside PancakeSwap

opening.argument: Judge, the profit projection is tied to a purchase walkthrough. The speaker says the chart could yield 170% profit, then instructs viewers to put BNB into a wallet and confirm a transaction to buy the token. Even if the projection depends on a chart breakout, the video turns that possible gain into a concrete path for committing funds. That promise-action pairing is the strongest reason to treat this as a token-purchase solicitation.

citations.quote: About 170% profit in the future.
Type the amount of BNB inside your Metamask wallet in order to purchase this token.
And then click on confirm and then just confirm the transaction of metal mask like this You can buy this token

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls the projection conditional, but that does not separate it from the requested purchase: the speaker explicitly discusses buying the project while describing a huge pump. A research disclaimer does not erase the later wallet-and-transaction instructions. No completed transfer is needed to recognize a solicitation.

citations.quote: If you want to buy this project, you can see a huge pump in here.
do your own research before buying any coins mentioned in the video.
Type the amount of BNB inside your Metamask wallet in order to purchase this token.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The purchase instructions are real, but the return estimate is presented through chart conditions, including resistance levels that must be broken. The speaker also tells viewers to do their own research and says their profit or loss is their own. A forecast alongside a standard exchange walkthrough does not, on this evidence, establish deception about the token or its returns.

citations.quote: If you break this resistance so we will touch our target
do your own research before buying any coins mentioned in the video.
It's your money and it will be your loss and profit.

opening.argument: Judge, assess the signals together. The title pairs an invitation to buy $DOGS with a striking percentage claim, while the narration projects 170% profit within an approximate one- or two-month period. At the point of exchange, the sampled swap screen itself displays a High Risk marker. None of these signals alone proves a scam, but their combination makes the upbeat return framing especially concerning: viewers are shown an actionable token purchase while prominent risk sits alongside unusually large upside claims.

citations.quote: Buy $DOGS on Pancakeswap | Create DAPPs and NFTs | 9700% wow
About 170% profit in the future. It takes time.. whether 1 month time or 2 months.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense says the estimate is conditional and no deception has been established. But that answer treats each cue in isolation. The video pairs a large projected gain with buying instructions, and the displayed swap interface marks the trade High Risk. The issue is whether the overall presentation encourages purchase despite those warning signs, not whether a transaction is shown as completed.

citations.quote: About 170% profit in the future.
Type the amount of BNB inside your Metamask wallet in order to purchase this token.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those are reasons for caution, not proof of a scam. The title does not say what its 9700% figure measures; the spoken profit projection depends on a chart breakout. The High Risk marker is visible on the exchange screen rather than concealed. The cited material supports a speculative, risky token discussion, but does not establish that the speaker fabricated the opportunity or guaranteed a return.

citations.quote: So if we break this pattern in the chart, then our target of the price chart is 0.08×0.7429

opening.argument: Judge, the review framing should be weighed against what the viewer is led to do. The speaker opens by promising a complete review, but also declares 100% potential for the project. The token's site presents a Buy Now control, and the speaker later walks through entering BNB and confirming a wallet transaction. Technical features and chart discussion make the presentation sound analytical; the resulting sequence still steers a viewer from favorable claims to a specific token purchase.

citations.quote: in this video I will give you complete review of Dogecoin Network
i can see see 100% potential to this project
Type the amount of BNB inside your Metamask wallet in order to purchase this token.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the video covers utility and chart analysis. That context also supplies the case for buying: after favorable project claims, the speaker gives the token contract-address route and directs viewers to PancakeSwap. Calling the material educational does not change the promotional function of that sequence, even without evidence that anyone completed a transfer.

citations.quote: Make sure to copy the BSC address from here and then go to your PancakeSwap for this token.
Now how to buy this token inside PancakeSwap

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A favorable review can promote a token without being a scam. The speaker also examines its price chart and identifies resistance levels, rather than presenting a purchase as a guaranteed payoff. The description explicitly denies acting as a financial adviser and urges viewers to research coins before buying. The prosecution establishes promotional intent, but its citations do not establish deceptive conduct.
